title: Young Turk Revolution
summary: In July 1908 the Committee of Union and Progress, a movement of army officers and educated Ottomans, forced Sultan Abdulhamid II to restore the Ottoman constitution of 1876. The revolution began on 3 July when Major Ahmed Niyazi led soldiers into the mountains of Macedonia; on 24 July the sultan issued a rescript restoring the constitution, opening a brief period of parliamentary politics.

uncertainty.note: Start and end from Imperial Ottoman; the National Herald records proclamations of the constitution on 23 July.

as_recorded.value: On 24 July 1908, the sultan issued a rescript restoring the constitution

where.historical_name: Constantinople, capital of the Ottoman Empire (proxy pin: the revolt began in Macedonia and spread across the empire)

importance.justification: Restored the Ottoman constitution and parliament and began the empire's Second Constitutional Era.

reviewer_note: Place is a proxy (Istanbul). Least sure of the sourcing quality of Imperial Ottoman; its dates match the National Herald account.
